::: project-summary
**Objective —** Demonstrate reproducible regression-modelling workflows for epidemiological and ecological data.

**Methods —** Exploratory analysis, linear and generalised regression, model diagnostics, and visualisation.

**Tools —** R (tidyverse, tidymodels, ggplot2).

*This page is a methods demonstration and is being expanded.*
:::

# Introduction

## Data {.larger style="font:bold"}

I start it with the penguins dataset from @palmerpenguins package [@corsi2021]

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#| label: load-package
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(gt)
glimpse(penguins)

```

## Species

@fig-bill-dims-species is a scatter plot of species of penguins

```{r}
#| label: fig-bill-dims-species
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-asp: 0.6
#| fig-alt: |
#|      A scatter plot
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: | 
#|    A scatter plot
#| output-location: slide
#| code-copy: true 
#| code-overflow: scroll

ggplot(penguins,
       aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm,
           color = species, shape = species)
       )+
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal()+
  #scale_color_continuous()+
  labs(x= "Bill length (mm)", y="Bill depth (mm)")

```

## Penguins

@tbl-penguins-top10 below shows first 10 penguins from the dataset.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-penguins-top10
#| tbl-cap: First 10 penguins
penguins|>
  slice_head(n=10)|>
  select(species, island, bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm)|> 
  gt()
```
